Sysvar and return-data syscalls for the VM, plus sibling-instruction queries.

# Purpose
This file implements Solana VM syscall handlers for reading sysvars and related runtime data, and for writing return data. Each function follows the VM syscall interface, checks that the VM runs inside an instruction context, charges compute units, validates output pointers, translates VM addresses to host addresses, and copies data from the runtime into guest memory. The sysvar handlers include [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_clock_sysvar`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_clock_sysvar>), [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_epoch_schedule_sysvar`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_epoch_schedule_sysvar>), [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_rent_sysvar`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_rent_sysvar>), [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_last_restart_slot_sysvar`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_last_restart_slot_sysvar>), [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_epoch_rewards_sysvar`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_epoch_rewards_sysvar>), and the generic [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_sysvar`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_sysvar>), which reads a sysvar by public key and offset.

The file also provides syscalls that expose transaction and execution state, such as [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_epoch_stake`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_epoch_stake>), [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_stack_height`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_stack_height>), [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_return_data`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_return_data>), [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_set_return_data`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_set_return_data>), and [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_processed_sibling_instruction`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_get_processed_sibling_instruction>). These functions read stake data from the bank, return the current instruction stack height, store or fetch transaction return data, and query earlier instructions in the same stack level. The code uses runtime context objects such as `fd_exec_instr_ctx_t`, `fd_exec_txn_ctx_t`, bank state, sysvar cache accessors, and VM memory translation helpers to implement the external syscall interface used by programs running in the VM.
